findings.claim: remove_member calls group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the existing Group#remove helper (app/models/group.rb:276), which skips the per-row cleanup. The removed user's primary_group_id is not cleared, so the group still shows as post flair via post_serializer.rb:96-102. groups.user_count (the counter_cache on GroupUser) is probably not decremented either. add_members uses group.add, so the two endpoints are also inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Reasoned, not run. A has_many :through delete removes the join rows with delete_all and runs no callbacks. The old path (usernames= -> destroy_deletions, group.rb:285-293) and Group#remove both destroy each row and null primary_group_id. The new spec at spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:118-130 checks only a live group.users.count. The counter-cache part comes from the seats' memory of Rails 4.1.8 and was not checked against the gem source. OCR says it is certain about primary_group_id and less certain about the counter. Suggested red test: set user.update_columns(primary_group_id: group.id), call remove_member, then expect user.reload.primary_group_id to be nil and group.reload.user_count to be 0.
findings.reason: Accepted. Four seats agree, and three hold it Important on correctness. Ponytail rated it Minor on the lean axis only. Before fixing, make the suggested spec red on the pinned code, then route the removal through Group#remove and add the primary_group_id reset there. The red test has not been executed (benchmark mode).

verifier.reason: The main defect is real, but part of the claim is wrong: Group#remove (app/models/group.rb:276-278) only destroys GroupUser rows and never clears primary_group_id. Only the removed usernames= → destroy_deletions path did that (group.rb:291), so switching to Group#remove would not fix it. The new remove_member (groups_controller.rb:649) calls group.users.delete(user_id) and has no primary_group_id cleanup, so the removed user still shows the group as flair (post_serializer.rb:96-102). The user_count claim depends on the Rails 4.1.8 gem source, which is not in the repo, so it is unverified here.

findings.claim: The public /groups/:name/members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 for every group. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200. The public route and template (discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11, discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6) have no pagination controls, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the template and route. Only admin/templates/group.hbs:15-19 got next/previous controls, and no pagination actions or controller exist under discourse/controllers/group/.
findings.reason: Accepted. Three seats agree. Needs a red test before the fix, for example a public members request for a group with more than 50 members that expects them all to be reachable. The red test has not been executed (benchmark mode).

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26 the patch now applies limit 50 to every group by default. Before, it returned all members of non-automatic groups and 200 for automatic ones. The public page loads only the first page: Group.findMembers in models/group.js sends limit 50 and offset 0, and group-members.js.es6:11 calls it once. templates/group/members.hbs has no next/previous controls, and there is no group-members controller or view, so members after the 50th cannot be reached.

findings.claim: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is off by one whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit. With 50 members and limit 50 the pager shows 1/2, and Next loads an empty page at offset 50. The correct formula is Math.ceil(user_count / limit), which also removes the == 0 guard. Related: removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page because findMembers keeps the old offset.
findings.evidence: Reasoned arithmetic: Math.floor(50/50)+1 === 2 while Math.ceil(50/50) === 1. There is no QUnit test in the patch.
findings.reason: Accepted. Four seats agree. Severity was normalised to Important: the correctness seats split (open-code-review Important, superpowers Minor) and the higher rating was kept. Red test: a QUnit or arithmetic check that totalPages is 1 for 50 members at limit 50. Not executed (benchmark mode).

verifier.reason: In admin-group.js.es6:13, totalPages = Math.floor(50/50)+1 = 2, so showingLast (line 17) is false on page 1. The next action (line 33) then sets offset to min(0+50, 50) = 50 and calls findMembers, which fetches an empty second page; Math.ceil would give the correct count.

findings.claim: The patch breaks the public and admin API with no compatibility path and no documentation. create and update read top-level params[:name], params[:visible] and params[:alias_level] instead of group[...]. As a result, a legacy create gets a blank name and a 422, and a legacy update silently sets visible=false. group[usernames] is ignored. PATCH /admin/groups/:id with changes[add|delete] is gone. GET /groups/:name/members now returns {members, meta} instead of an array. The commit body is empty, which goes against CONTRIBUTING §5's requirement for a detailed description, so the breaking change is documented nowhere.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. See admin/groups_controller.rb:22-41 and 65-99, groups_controller.rb:28-35 and config/routes.rb:49-51. Suggested red test: the old spec `xhr :patch, :update, id: group.id, changes: {add: user2.username}` no longer adds the user. Whether the discourse_api gem uses the PATCH changes shape was not checked.
findings.reason: Accepted. Three seats agree. Merged with mattpocock's finding on commit 060cda7772: same claim, an undocumented breaking admin API change, raised under the CONTRIBUTING commit-message standard. Make the legacy PATCH spec red first. The resolution is either a compat path or a documented breaking change in the commit body. Not executed (benchmark mode).

verifier.reason: The code matches the claim. In app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-44, create and update now read top-level params[:name], params[:visible] and params[:alias_level], and nothing reads group[...] or group[usernames]. A legacy update therefore sets visible = (nil == "true"), which is false, and a legacy create gets a blank name that the name-format validator should reject with render_json_error. The PATCH changes[add|delete] handling (update_patch) is deleted, so a PATCH request reaches update and ignores changes. app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:29-35 now returns {members, meta} instead of an array. Only the in-repo JS client was updated (group.js), I could not check the commit body from here, and no external API consumers were checked.

findings.claim: add_members calls group.add(user) (users.push, which inserts at once) without checking membership. Adding a user who is already a member violates the unique index on group_users(group_id, user_id) and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which returns a 500. Users earlier in the list stay committed because the loop is not in a transaction. The UI never clears the input, which makes this easy to hit.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. See group.rb:272 and db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9. Suggested red test: group.add(u), then xhr :put, :add_members with usernames: u.username, then response.should be_success.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, below the three-seat threshold, so it is not reported or fixed in this loop. Both correctness seats rate it Important, so it should be prioritised for follow-up.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored: no build, rspec, jshint or QUnit result backs any finding. Every red test and command named above is a seat suggestion that has not been executed. No spec exists: findings were measured against the commit title and the prior behaviour. The standards axis did run, against CONTRIBUTING.md, .jshintrc and .editorconfig. Not verified: Rails 4.1.8 has_many :through delete and counter-cache semantics (all seats worked from memory), the request shape used by the discourse_api gem, and Ember template rendering (no browser check). Files skipped or reviewed shallowly: mattpocock did not review admin_base.scss, user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs or admin-group-selector.hbs in depth, and checked only that the new client.en.yml keys are used. superpowers did not review user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs or admin-group-selector.hbs in depth, and reviewed admin_base.scss for the .form-horizontal move only. ponytail did not review config/locales/client.en.yml and only skimmed spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb. open-code-review reviewed all 16 files, reviewing manually the 4 that its tool excluded (three .es6 files and the spec). Every file in the patch was therefore covered in depth by at least one seat. No rejections: nothing in the seat reports disproves another seat's claim, so no verifier was needed. No fix rounds were run, so nothing has converged.
